name: Wanderburg — Low-poly 3D (shipped)
description: THE presentation the game ships: a perspective camera over the rolling fortress, hand-built low-poly meshes, toon bands with environment ink edges, no silhouette outline (on convex hand-built meshes the inverted hull wins the depth tie and paints the object black), no shadow map — every hull drops its own blob shadow. Sun, sky and fog come from the biome (js/Content.js), so the variant pins only the shading model. Camera pose and the zoom range mirror Constants.js (CAMERA_*); the zoom itself stays authored by the game (CAMERA_ZOOM / CAMERA_ZOOM_MOBILE). Draw load, measured on a full valley (verify/deploy.mjs, C-6 revision 2): ~900 base + ~250 ink unique enabled mesh instances; GL draws per frame swing with the camera/culling moment (365-1230 measured: a zoomed-in framing culls half the valley, a full-visibility moment draws every instance exactly once). The old \"4-8k draws/frame\" was an artifact of the CUMULATIVE device._drawCallsPerFrame counter (nothing resets it without profiling), and ink edges were not drawn at all until the engine fix of _inkEdgeMesh (GPU index buffers lock() to a raw ArrayBuffer; setPositions builds a PLANAR vertex buffer whose element stride is not fmt.size) — PlayArcEngine b813027. maxDrawCalls states the profile canon as the ENTITY count (900 base drawable instances — the kit's \"batch or instance them\"); the gate guards draws/frame by the RATIO to the census (a leak draws instances dead or twice), and WORLD3D_TOON_INK=1 (actors only) or 0 is the mobile lever. Every entity is SELF-PRESENTED (GAME_SPEC.entities declare representation "none"): js/WanderView.js + js/WanderMesh.js build the meshes on the kit engine layer, so the pipeline binds no second copy of anything.
